precepts.text: While they beheld, he was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight. Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? This same Jesus shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.
precepts.point: But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me. Churches don't read that; churches will look at that and go, no, we're not reading that in Sunday school. You know what it means further? You ain't going to just be able to do what you want to do. You was put on this earth to do what the Most High and Christ said, and if you don't do that, then there's no reason for you to live. He said, if you don't want to do what you were created for, bring him before me and end his existence.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
Christ spake this parable “because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and because they thought that the kingdom of God should immediately appear.” A lot of people thought the kingdom was coming at that time. That's why Paul later said, let no man deceive you: that day shall not come except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed.

“A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.” The far country in this context is the heavens. Acts shows him going: “while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.”

And Acts shows him returning: “Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.” The nobleman is Christ. He went into heaven to receive the kingdom, and he is coming back, and when he returns he calls his servants to account.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.” What are the pounds? God's word.

David says: “Therefore I love thy commandments above gold; yea, above fine gold.” The commandments are more precious than gold, so the money the nobleman hands his servants is his word: the knowledge, the understanding, the faith he bestowed on each of us.

Occupy till I come means do something with it until he returns. When he comes back he wants to know “how much every man had gained by trading”: how much each one went out and taught the word. The servant who laid his pound up in a napkin kept the word to himself, and that is how he is judged.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“But his citizens hated him, and sent a message after him, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us.” Who hated him? Mark shows it: “the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.”

Rejected is the word to highlight. The elders, the chief priests and the scribes rejected him: back then it was the scribes and Pharisees and those that followed them who said, we will not have this man to reign over us.

Today there are no groups called scribes and Pharisees, but the same spirit is here. They are the Christians, they are the Muslims; they fall into this. They reject his reign, and at the end of the parable the King says what becomes of them: “But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.”

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.” That's what we all want: dominion. Revelation says the same: “And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers.”

We're not going to play with the nations. We've got to teach them to honor the King of kings. We've got to teach them the civil law, the ceremonial law, the dietary law, the moral law, and the history of Israel too. They are not going to be glorifying China any more, or the white man; they are going to glorify the history of Israel.

Just one city is too much to handle in this body and mind we have now. That's why it's exciting to read this: the Lord is going to have to change this. Some of you have problems dealing with that one black woman you've got right now, and you're talking about being lord over five cities. Being faithful in a very little now is what earns the authority then.

precepts.why:
The nobleman gave the pounds “that he might know how much every man had gained by trading.” The trading is going out teaching the word. It is business: “Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord.”

This is talking about God's business. If it were the white man's business, you wouldn't be slothful, because you've got to eat, you've got to have a place to live. But in God's business people get slothful. Be fervent in spirit, on fire in spirit, serving the Lord.

The first servant's pound gained ten pounds and the second's gained five, and they were rewarded with cities. The servant who was slothful in the Lord's business laid his pound up in a napkin and gained nothing.

He taketh away: take you away and kill you, that's what it's talking about. And every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit. You got to be purged to bring forth more fruit. There's things in us: I got to cut this off, cut that person off from you, cut this out of your soul, your spirit, so you can bear more fruit.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“Take from him the pound, and give it to him that hath ten pounds.” Imagine the order, like the king in Game of Thrones giving orders to the men next to the throne. It's pure order. “For I say unto you, That unto every one which hath shall be given; and from him that hath not, even that he hath shall be taken away from him.”

John shows the same judgment: “Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away.” Not bearing fruit means you're not increasing in the fruits of the spirit. You're the same grimy person you were five years back; there's no change in you, no transformation. It goes for men and women: the same gossiper, murmurer, complainer you were five years ago, just here with fringes and a border of blue. He taketh away means he takes you away and kills you.

“and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit.” You've got to be purged to bring forth more fruit. There are things in us that have to be cut: cut this off, cut that person off from you, cut this out of your soul and your spirit, so you can bear more fruit.

We've seen it. Brothers came among us with certain skills and did not expand on them, so the Most High, like musical chairs, moved them out of the way. Other brothers came in, took that office and ran with it, and you don't hear anything about the men who were here with the ability to do just that.

precepts.why:
The third servant came with excuses: “Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin: For I feared thee, because thou art an austere man.” And the Lord answered, “Out of thine own mouth will I judge thee, thou wicked servant.”

“A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will.” For every solution, these people have five excuses. The wicked servant would not own that he did nothing with what he was given; he blamed his lord for being austere.

Your excuses are not going to fly with Christ. He doesn't care about your excuses. He knew exactly what the servant knew: “Thou knewest that I was an austere man, taking up that I laid not down, and reaping that I did not sow.” If you knew it, you should have done something with it.

precepts.why:
“Wherefore then gavest not thou my money into the bank, that at my coming I might have required mine own with usury?” This is the bank: the congregation. Usury means interest. So when Christ comes back, he wants interest on what he gave each of us.

Paul shows the great house: “But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The bank is his great house. Your work, your love, your zeal, your understanding: bring it into the bank, the congregation.

“If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.” The servant who brings what he was given into the house and purges himself becomes a vessel of honour, fit for the master's use when he returns and requires his own with usury.

precepts.text: But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me. Everybody that's against what Christ said is an enemy of Christ, and that includes our people. You fathers and mothers are trying to rule over your children to keep them from going astray, and they say, I'm not having that; the hell with what you got to say. In the wilderness, Christ will be teaching the commandments face to face, and those still refusing, he said, bring them before me.
precepts.point: And it shall come to pass, that when any shall yet prophesy, then his father and his mother that begat him shall say unto him, Thou shalt not live; and shall thrust him through when he prophesieth. Why would his own father and mother do that? Because they will have already witnessed how Christ dealt with the rebellious. Once those parents see that Christ isn't playing, that's how the parents are going to be moving. I'm going back to you brothers and sisters with sons and daughters that refuse to change: don't put your life on the line for wickedness that refuses to repent.

note.label: In a Game of Fools Without The Rules

precepts.why:
Zechariah says that when any shall yet prophesy lies, “his father and his mother that begat him shall say unto him, Thou shalt not live”, and “shall thrust him through when he prophesieth.” Why would his own father and mother do that? Because they will have already witnessed how Christ dealt with the rebellious. Christ said it: “But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.”

Everybody that is against what Christ said is an enemy of Christ, and that includes our people. You fathers and mothers try to rule over your children to keep them from going astray, and they say, I'm not having that; I'm doing my own thing; the hell with what you got to say, mama; the hell with that Bible. They refuse the correction of their fathers and mothers ruling over them, and they would not that Christ and his law should reign over them.

This happens in the wilderness. Christ will be teaching the commandments face to face, and some will still tell him, I ain't doing this, I ain't doing that. Christ said, bring them here, and kill them right in front of my feet.

Once those parents see that Christ ain't playing, that is how they will be moving: you want to put my head on the chopping block? You will die right now. So to you brothers and sisters with sons and daughters that refuse to change: don't put your life on the line for wickedness that refuses to repent. We pray our brothers and sisters get their minds right now, so they don't end up there.

note.label: John 4: The Woman at the Well and the Nobleman's Son

precepts.why:
“Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father.” Jerusalem itself was to be laid level with the ground. Christ wept over the city: “If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes.”

“For the days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side, And shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.”

Not one stone upon another. That is why the hour was coming when men would neither worship in that mountain nor at Jerusalem: the place itself would be laid even with the ground.

Just to prove the point. “When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” See that? They thought it was in: will you restore the kingdom to Israel? Now how come the churches don't read that and go, "No, they made a mistake. It's for everybody"? The hell is this?

Here's another one, with John the Baptist. And anybody that thinks John the Baptist was a wicked negro, you're on crack. “Now when John had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples, And said unto him, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?” Why'd he ask that? John was in prison. He thought deliverance was at that time. That's why he was talking greasy to Herod: remember Herod walked in with his brother's wife and John was bold, it's unlawful for you to have your brother's wife, and they arrested him and put him in jail. So he's thinking, I'm good, Christ is going to deliver me out of here. But that wasn't the time.

“Jesus answered and said unto them, Go and shew John again those things which ye do hear and see:” To encourage John. “The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.” Here it comes. “And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.” He was telling John, don't be offended, because this is not the time for deliverance. This is the time for me to be sacrificed. Everybody thought it was going to be the same thing; nobody wanted to hear the sacrifice stuff. All Israel wanted the deliverance part, the vengeance part, but that was not the time.

This goes back to the point that they all thought deliverance was coming right then, at that time. Paul said, let no man deceive you. “Now we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ,” So the subject matter is the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ. “and by our gathering together unto him,” And the gathering of the twelve tribes unto Christ. “That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us,” Concerning what? “as that the day of Christ is at hand.” Y'all see that? People going around saying this is the time, this is the time. Paul had to make it sure and certain: this is not the time.

“Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come,” What day? The second coming of Christ. “except there come a falling away first,” Meaning all twelve tribes must fall. During this time all twelve tribes did not fall yet. Judah was still in the land, Benjamin, Levi, and remnants of the others. They did not all fall, not yet. But remember Christ prophesied, and they shall fall by the edge of the sword. That was 70 AD. The twelve tribes must all fall first and go into captivity. “and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition;” The white man got to be revealed that he's the devil the Bible speaks of. So Paul had to make it clear: listen, stop. Christ ain't coming in this time period. Things got to happen. All Israel got to fall and go into captivity. Nobody wanted to hear that.

What does it mean when it says he went into a far country? “And when he had spoken these things, while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.” So he went into the heavens, to the true tabernacle. That's where Christ went. That's the far country of the nobleman.
The servants. “But thou, Israel, art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend.” Everybody's not the servants of the Lord.

The Christians just get on my nerve with their lies: "Everybody's the servants of the Lord." No, they're not. “For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.” So everybody is not the servants of the Lord. The ten servants are Israel.

The ten pounds. Pounds is money; this is money. What is it going into? “Therefore I love thy commandments above gold; yea, above fine gold.” So these pounds represent something so precious, which is the word of God, the commandments.

The citizens that hated him: who hated Christ? You hear Christians go, "He came unto his own and his own received him not." Shut up. That ain't talking about all the Israelites. “And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes,” That's who hated Christ. That's who rejected him.

Having received the kingdom: there's a lot implied in that. If you don't read the Old Testament prophecies, you'll just read this parable and go, "Oh yeah, he just came back to the kingdom." No, a lot took place between that.

“For, behold, the Lord will come with fire,” He's coming with fire. “and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire. For by fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh: and the slain of the Lord shall be many.” So Christ is going to kill a lot of people to receive his kingdom.

“They that sanctify themselves, and purify themselves in the gardens” The gardens is religions and their churches. “behind one tree in the midst, eating swine’s flesh,” Swine's flesh is pork, hog. “and the abomination,” That's monkey hands, iguana, rat, stuff like that. “and the mouse,” That's rabbit stew, possum stew, things like that. “shall be consumed together, saith the Lord.” This is what happens before he takes the kingdom. It's going to be a lot of killing.

Showing you what happens before he takes the kingdom. “And there was war in heaven:” There was what? War in heaven. “Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels,” So Satan is going to fight against Michael and his angels. So Satan's going to have who? America, Europe, China, Russia; they're all going to fight against the Lord. “And prevailed not; neither was their place found any more in heaven. And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.”

Here it is. “And I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.” Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God. That's the receiving of the kingdom. So there's going to be war and turmoil before that comes.

That he might know how much every man had gained by trading: what did you do with the understanding I imparted to you? “Wherefore we labour, that, whether present or absent, we may be accepted of him.” We all want to be accepted of Christ. “For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ;” Every man, every woman. And this is what the parable's talking about: what did you do with what I gave you? “that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.” Whether it be good or bad.
“So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God.” That's right. Every servant is called to account for what he did with the pounds.

“He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.” So the first servant, faithful in a very little with his pound, is given authority over ten cities.

Have thou authority over ten cities. “And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations:” That's have thou authority over ten cities. “And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers:”

Look at what he's actually saying in Luke 19:17. You know how difficult it is with your family: you family men trying to get your wife to come to this truth, your kids out of order, you got to try to get the household together. Now imagine trying to organize a whole city, and not just one city, ten cities. That means you got to teach them the dietary law, moral law, civil law, ceremonial law. This is what the servant with the napkin is doing. “A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will.” Them old excuse makers.
